conviction_note: abs_move 5.0 (proxy 4.14, raised because a forecast decision is likely at this H1; the last two forecast cuts traded -5.15 and -7.4) times p_up 42 gives -0.8. The findings sum to -1.0, mostly one company-level fact: the 76bn OP plan needs an H2 far above anything this company has delivered. That fact is partly priced through eight sell-side target cuts and -8% over 20 days. A weak yen and a possible group buyback are the offsets.
bar: FY3/2027 operating profit: IFIS consensus 75.6bn OP / 82.7bn pretax / 47.9bn net (as of 2026-10-28, https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/reportAnalyst?bcode=3116) against the company plan of 76.0bn / 80.0bn / 46.0bn, already cut from 80bn on 2026-07-31 (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260731/140120260727500061.pdf). The bar is the consensus, which sits at or above the plan. My print_vs_bar is the FY OP guide I expect after this release (around 72-73bn) relative to 75.6bn.
positioning_check: JPX short register 2026-10-28: 0.0% disclosed (no position at or above 0.5%), change 0.0 (baseline, https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html). Margin ratio 3.31 (kabutan, 2026-10-29), so leveraged retail is moderately long and a visible miss still has sellers. No option skew exists. The sell side has cut targets eight times since 2026-07-16, with two Underweight/sell downgrades (2026-08-20 and 2026-09-09, TP 2,000); rating consensus 2.50 (https://kabuyoho.jp/reportNews?bcode=3116&cat=4). Run-up -8.04% over 20 days and -3.81% over 5 days; -1.5% on 10-28, the day peers Tokai Rika and Chuo Hatsujo printed.

findings.finding: The FY3/2027 OP plan of 76.0bn (cut from 80bn at Q1) needs about 60bn in Q2-Q4 after a 15.9bn Q1 (20.9% progress, against 23.4% at the same point last year). Last year the company cut at H1 (80bn to 75bn) and then delivered 53.9bn, with H2 OP of only 16.9bn because Q4 lost 6.3bn. FY24 and FY25 plans were also missed by 15-38%. IFIS consensus (75.6bn OP, 82.7bn pretax) still sits at or above the plan, so a second cut at this H1 lands below the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two forecast cuts both traded badly. 2025-10-31: H1 OP +10% but the FY OP was cut 80 to 75bn; traders.co.jp headline '後場急落', baseline move -5.15%. 2026-07-31: FY cut 80 to 76bn; '後場急落', baseline -7.4%. A held guide on 2026-02-03 traded '後場上げ幅拡大'.
findings.source_date: 2026-10-28 (revision history and consensus as of 2026-10-28); Q1 短信 https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260731/140120260727500061.pdf dated 2026-07-31
findings.why_not_priced: The IFIS consensus has not moved below the plan (82.7bn pretax against the company's 80bn), so the published bar does not model a cut. If a cut were fully priced, consensus would sit under the plan, and the stock would not have traded down 5-7% on each of the last two cuts. Partly priced: eight sell-side target cuts and -8% over 20 days.
findings.independence: The company revision record (kabuyoho) and the Q1 短信 (TDnet) are two documents carrying one fact, counted once here. The volume and peer findings below bear on the same revision decision but come from different sources.

findings.finding: Toyota's global production turned down in the quarter Toyota Boshoku is reporting: July -2.1% and August -5.9% y/y, overseas production -7.6% in August (fourth straight decline), Toyota China sales -24.3% in July and -22.8% in August. Toyota Boshoku's China segment OP had already halved in Q1 (2.0bn, -50.4%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-07-31): China volume was cited as the reason for the cut and the stock fell 7.4% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: Toyota's monthly production data is public and the stock fell 8% into the print. What may remain is the size of the China hit in the segment table and whether management cites it to cut the plan.
findings.independence: Kyodo via Kumanichi, 2026-09-29, carries the same August numbers (https://kumanichi.com/articles/2040803), so it is one dataset. Toyota Boshoku's own Q1 短信 confirms China exposure and the Q1 China OP drop.

findings.finding: Two Toyota-group parts makers printed on 2026-10-28. Chuo Hatsujo (5992) cut its FY OP 45% (3.3bn to 1.8bn), citing 'China production cuts beyond our assumption', NA tariffs and delayed inflation recovery. Tokai Rika (6995) held its guide, but H1 OP fell 17.7% and Japan segment OP fell 71% on raw-material costs and fixed costs. Both stocks fell: Tokai Rika 2,990 open to 2,911 close on 10-28, then 2,833 on 10-29; Chuo Hatsujo -4.4% on 10-28.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for 3116 specifically. 3116 itself fell 1.5% on 2026-10-28 (2,085.5 open to 2,041.5 close), the day these peers printed, and is down another 1.1% this morning.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: 3116 has already traded down about 2.6% since these releases. The unpriced part is whether Toyota Boshoku, with Q1 already flagging China and Middle East materials, cuts the plan the way Chuo Hatsujo did.
findings.independence: Tokai Rika's H1 短信 is a separate document from a different company (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20261028/140120261027557204.pdf). Its Japan-segment raw-material comment matches Toyota Boshoku's own Q1 mention of '中東情勢に伴う市況影響'.

findings.finding: The yen ran well weaker than the company's 150 JPY/USD assumption all through the quarter: 162.59 to 157.58 in July, about 159.7 at end-August, 157.41 at end-September (low 152.88), and 157.9 this morning. That is also far weaker than about 147 a year ago. Q1 already credited FX as a positive. A re-set FX assumption gives management room to offset volume and hold the plan.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separable in the record. The 2026-02-03 hold of the FY guide traded up ('後場上げ幅拡大').
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro data, but the company's 150 assumption was set on 2026-07-31 and nobody outside knows the sensitivity or whether management will move the assumption. A cautious house could keep 150 and let FX sit as a buffer. I am not sizing it as certain.
findings.independence: Toyota Boshoku Q1 短信 (2026-07-31) names 為替影響 as a profit and revenue tailwind; kabutan header 2026-10-29 shows USD/JPY 157.89.

findings.finding: Toyota Industries, now taken private, still held 4.13% of Toyota Boshoku as a policy holding at its 2026-05-20 large-holding filing. Toyota-group peer Tokai Rika paired its H1 on 10-28 with a 2.9% ToSTNeT-3 buyback-and-cancel. Toyota Boshoku has 278.5bn of cash and absorbed Denso's 3.05% stake in FY3/2024 with a 20bn buyback. A buyback announced with this H1 is possible; no document says one is coming.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No buyback has been announced at a print in the available record. Tokai Rika's buyback did not stop its stock falling (2,990 to 2,833 over about one session).
findings.source_date: 2026-05-20 (Toyota Industries filing); Tokai Rika notice https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20261028/140120261027557246.pdf dated 2026-10-28
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody has reported a sale intention for the 3116 stake, and the stock trades at PBR 0.73 with a 4.3% yield and no buyback premium visible. If the market expected a buyback, 3116 would not have lagged on the peer-buyback day (-1.5% on 10-28). This is inference, sized small.
findings.independence: Chuo Hatsujo also announced a 15bn buyback (a 12bn ToSTNeT-3) on 10-28 (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20261028/140120261028558281.pdf), but its 18% activist holder makes it a different case.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision expected? Likely: the company revised at H1 in each of the last four years and cut at Q1 this year, and a second cut (OP to roughly 70-73bn) is my base case against IFIS 75.6bn. FX at about 157-158 vs the 150 assumption is the route to a hold. Returns? Dividend 43/43 planned (DOE about 3.2%, policy 3%+), so no raise needed; a buyback is possible but unsourced. New-year guide? No, this is H1. Quarter vs own 進捗率? Q1 was 20.9% of FY OP against 23.4% last year, and last year's H1 was 49% of a plan that was then cut and missed.

baseline_tension: The negative findings agree with the run-up (-8% over 20 days, -3.8% over 5) and the sell-side tone, so much of them is held. priced_lean is +0.14 (mild up, from the run-up term). The strongest positive this release could carry is a held FY plan with the FX assumption moved toward 155, plus a buyback absorbing Toyota Industries' 4.13%. I looked for both: the FX room is real and sourced, the buyback is unsourced. After eight target cuts a cut could also trade as 悪材料出尽くし, which is why p_up sits at 42 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (negative resting on a public series): the Toyota monthly production finding shrank from -0.5 to -0.3, and the peer read-through, public since 10-28 and already partly traded by 3116, from -0.5 to -0.3. The guidance finding stays at -1.2 because the release itself adds the revision decision, the exception rule 1 names.

Rule 2 (negatives outnumber positives): I had already looked for the held-forecast/FX and buyback positives, so the findings' sizes did not change. p_up moved from 40 to 42 for the 悪材料出尽くし risk after eight target cuts.
Net effect: impact_sum -1.4 to -1.0; expected_move -1.0 to -0.8; abs_move unchanged at 5.0.
